answer.rationale: memory_b5 confirms read-replica routing recovered write latency the same day and reduced primary load from report/dashboard traffic. p99 on the write path climbing 5x during settlement peak is consistent with the primary carrying reads (dashboard/analytics queries) on top of heavy writes — b5 is exactly the prior analogue. The security patch must not be reverted, so rollback_release and add_capacity would either violate compliance or not directly address the read/write contention. Regional failover (b2) restores latency fast during regional degradation, but there's no signal here of a regional fault — this is a primary-write-path saturation under peak load, which b2 did not address. Circuit breaker (b4) is for a partner dependency outage, not the present symptom. Routing read traffic to replicas targets the root cause without touching the release, preserves the security patch, and matches a proven prior outcome. Verify b5 (primary analogue) and b2 (to rule out regional failover as an alternative before committing). One intervention: route non-transactional reads to read replicas now, monitor p99 write latency; if not recovering in next window, escalate to add_capacity or failover.
